title: There’s No Way To Block Podcasts
review:
There is no way to block individual podcasts, and using the “Not Interested” button simply doesn’t work. The same 3-4 podcasts are recommended ad nauseum despite not being followed or listened too, and there is no way to remove or hide them. Topic you hate? Too bad! Here’s 10 more podcasts about it we think you’ll love, and no way to toggle away from them. This happens daily, I must’ve clicked “Not Interested” on hundreds of episodes from the same podcast at this point.

After over 10 years of premium membership and reaching out several times to support, I went ahead and cancelled my plan. Why would I want to come back to a platform that keeps recommending me things that I hate?

1). It will consistently play episodes from a podcast’s regular feed when I only ever listen to the Patron feed. I haven’t listened to the main feed in years besides the few seconds that the app autoplays. Yet it still does it every single week when a new episode is out. 

2). Autoplays new episodes of podcasts that I’m not caught up on. If I’ve started a podcast from the beginning and add it to my shows, there really should be a way for the app to recognize where I’ve left off.  And if it wants to autoplay that podcast it can pick up where I’ve left off. Again, I’ve never manually played the new episodes of these shows, but every single week Spotify tries to autoplay them.

3). It plays episodes that I’ve already listened to. I will listen to a new episode of a podcast, finish, move on to another show’s new episode, then it will autoplay the first episode I’ve already listened to. 

4). Just because I listen to one episode of a show doesn’t mean I need every single new episode to be added to my queue. It would be nice to add a way to exclude shows from the autoplay queue. 

None of this is life shattering, but it’s extremely annoying having to reach into my pocket and fix the app’s mistakes when I’m trying to listen to stuff while I’m busy. And it’s not an issue I was having even a year ago.

I accidentally added my entire playlist to the same playlist, which created a bunch of duplicates and made my playlist 23 hours long 😭. It was really frustrating. I also tried deleting the duplicates, but it ended up deleting all copies of those songs instead, so I had to add them back again.

I was wondering if you could bring back the feature where, if someone tries to add a duplicate song, a message pops up saying that the song is already in the playlist and prevents it from being added again. I would really appreciate it!

review: I’ve been using Spotify premium for several years now, but my hang up with the app has remained the same: download only mode. When I turn off my data or find myself in a place without signal the player fails in a variety of ways. My main problems are that if I pause it for more than a couple of minutes then press play again, it will play a couple of seconds before it stops playing indefinitely or until I reset the app. What’s worse, there have been a few times when it will display my downloaded stuff but will not play anything at all no matter what until I turn on my data and reset the app (which defeats the purpose of download mode). They may not seem like huge concerns, but they have definitely become quite annoying after so many years.

title: Mental Health Ads Incessant
review:
As a therapist, I’m well informed about the power of suggestion and how triggering it can be to hear about mental illness and cognitive disabilities. The repeated suggestion via advertisements isn’t just pushing a podcast— it’s telling me that the way I, as someone without ADHD, relate to the world is incorrect. That I should be perceiving the world from the perspective of someone who views the world differently. I’m all for mental health and I’m glad the content is out there for people it benefits. I ALSO expect to be able to opt out as someone who finds it extremely triggering, and despite stating I do not like the ad, I still hear it 15 times a day. It’s unacceptable. Mental health conditions impact everyone. Three of my closest friends have ADHD. It’s TRIGGERING and I need to be able to block it. 

It came on AGAIN as I typed this. Beyond repulsive. 

Going to leave Spotify if ad controls don’t become more customizable.

title: I swear it’s all freaking ads
review: Spotify remains my primary listening platform, but I swear the amount of ads is becoming absolutely absurd. You cannot listen to more than one song without getting an ad immediately afterwards, and it’s usually five ads in a row, not just one. They’re also embedded in my liked songs playlists, my homepage, EVERWHERE It’s like the equivalent of Pinterest’s homepage (don’t but even get me started about that) but you have to hear AND see the ads. Please just pick one. An app can be free without being garbage. Also for the number of ads you get, one would think they would do more 30 minutes of uninterrupted listening but I’m pretty sure that’s extinct now. Such a disappointment on so many levels, doesn’t feel like Spotify is focused on the consumer but just making money.

title: A Very Intuitive App
review:
I always use Spotify to create my playlists for my DJing gigs, college radio shows, and just in general for fun. I’ve been using Spotify for a few years at the time of this and it has become one of my favorite apps for discovering music, organizing playlists, and having all of my favorite songs in one place.

I especially love how easy it is to create and customize playlists for different events, Whether I’m putting together a playlist for a DJ gig, preparing music for my college radio show, or just making a playlist for myself, Spotify makes the whole process really simple.

The music discovery features are also great, and I’ve found so many artists and songs that I probably wouldn’t have discovered otherwise.

title: Great.. if you have money
review: It would be a 1.5 but that’s not an option apparently. Spotify is a great music app IF you have premium. But when you don’t have premium it’s genuinely hard to listen to music at all..  I mean come on, limited amount of times you get to choose the specific song you want to play? “Want to choose the songs you play? You can choose again tomorrow.” I mean what even is that? And when playing playlists, it doesn’t even choose songs in the playlist. Horrendous if you don’t have premium and not to mention the premium is just getting more and more expensive.. Was so loyal to Spotify but a day in without premium and I already don’t use the app anymore.
